# HeroGPUI — llms.txt

> UI library for Rust desktop applications. HeroUI's design system,
> implemented in Rust on GPUI — Zed's GPU-accelerated UI framework.
> 71 documented components, light and dark, fully typed.

## Overview

HeroGPUI implements HeroUI's design system in Rust: OKLCH semantic tokens,
layout tokens, and typed component builders for Windows, macOS and Linux.

- **Crate:** `herogpui` (the single dependency; re-exports GPUI itself)
- **Theme:** `herogpui-theme` — `ThemeProvider` global, `ActiveTheme` trait
  (`cx.colors()`, `cx.role(Color::Accent)`, `cx.layout()`)
- **Core:** `herogpui-core` — `Color`, `Variant`, `FieldVariant`, `Prominence`,
  `Backdrop`, `Size`, `SizeXl`, `Orientation`, `SelectionMode`, OKLCH math
- **Components:** `herogpui-components` — one module per `@heroui/*` package
- **Gallery:** `cargo run -p herogpui-gallery` or `cargo install --path gallery --locked` — living docs, the fifteen v3
  categories, theme switcher

**Scope note.** This file documents the current HeroUI design system only.
The previous major version used different names, and they do not exist here:
`content1..4` surface tokens, numbered 50–900 colour scales,
`primary`/`secondary` as colours, the `radius` prop, and the components
`Navbar`, `Image`, `User`, `Spacer`, `Code`, `Snippet`. Do not emit them.

## Installation

```toml
[dependencies]
herogpui = { git = "https://github.com/Porabuild/HeroGPUI" }
```

One dependency, and only one. Not on crates.io yet. `herogpui` is a facade over the GPUI crate
family: it depends on `gpui-pre` `=0.3.3` and `gpui-pre-platform` `=0.3.3` and
re-exports them, so `use herogpui::*;` is GPUI and `herogpui::application()`
opens the platform. Do not emit `gpui` or `gpui_platform` as dependencies of a
consuming crate, and never emit the unrelated crates.io `gpui` 0.2.2 crate.
(Zed does not publish `gpui` under that name; `gpui-pre` is zed-industries'
own prerelease publish of the same sources.)

Paths and the Cargo features that carry them:

| Path | Crate | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `herogpui::*` | `gpui` | always |
| `herogpui::platform`, `herogpui::application` | `gpui_platform` | always |
| `herogpui::web` | `gpui_platform` | always, `cfg(target_family = "wasm")` only |
| `herogpui::core` | `herogpui-core` | `core` (implied by `theme`) |
| `herogpui::theme` | `herogpui-theme` | `theme` (implied by `components`) |
| `herogpui::components`, `herogpui::*` | `herogpui-components` | `components` (default) |

`test-support` forwards `gpui/test-support` and `gpui_platform/test-support`;
`profiler` forwards `gpui/profiler`. `serde` forwards `herogpui-theme/serde`
and is off by default: `ThemeDocument` is a sparse JSON override applied
through `ThemeBuilder`, so derived hover / soft mixes stay live. There is no assets or icons feature — the
embedded icons are constants inside `herogpui-components` and arrive with
`components`.

```rust
use herogpui::*;

actions!(my_app, [Quit]);

struct MyRoot;

impl Render for MyRoot {
    fn render(&mut self, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> impl IntoElement {
        app_focus_root(
            div().size_full().bg(cx.colors().background).text_color(cx.colors().foreground),
            window,
            cx,
        )
    }
}

fn main() {
    application().with_assets(HeroGpuiAssets).run(|cx: &mut App| {
        herogpui::init(cx); // = ThemeProvider::init(cx), light + dark
        // or ThemeProvider::init_with(Theme::dark(), cx);
        let bounds = Bounds::centered(None, size(px(1280.), px(820.)), cx);
        cx.open_window(WindowOptions { window_bounds: Some(WindowBounds::Windowed(bounds)), ..Default::default() },
            |_, cx| cx.new(|_| MyRoot)).unwrap();
    });
}
```

Emit `herogpui::actions!`, not `gpui::actions!`: GPUI's own macro expands its
derive as the absolute path `gpui::Action`, which does not resolve when GPUI is
reached only through the facade. The facade re-implements it with
`$crate::Action`. Every GPUI *derive* macro (`Action`, `IntoElement`, `Render`,
`AppContext`, `VisualContext`) likewise expands to hard-coded `gpui::…` paths;
`use herogpui::*;` puts the name `gpui` in scope and they resolve. With a
selective import instead, add `use herogpui::gpui;` before deriving.

Eight names exist in both GPUI and HeroUI v3: `ColorSpace`, `FontWeight`,
`Menu`, `MenuItem`, `Orientation`, `Size`, `Surface`, `TextAlign`. At
`herogpui`'s root the HeroUI v3 spelling wins (`Size::Md`, not a width/height
pair); reach GPUI's through `gpui::` (`gpui::Size`, `gpui::FontWeight`).

`HeroGpuiAssets` embeds the `herogpui/icons/*.svg` files used by built-in
component chrome. Use `HeroGpuiAssets::with_fallback(MyAppAssets)` when the app
also has assets. Wrap the window's root element with
`app_focus_root(root, window, cx)` to enable Tab traversal, focus-visible state,
and root capture handlers. Tab traversal consumes the browser default so DOM focus stays in the GPUI input surface.

Set root bg/fg via tokens:

```rust
div().bg(cx.colors().background).text_color(cx.colors().foreground).font_family("Segoe UI")
```

Toggle: `herogpui::theme::toggle_light_dark(cx);` or `use_theme("dark", cx)` or
`set_theme(custom, cx)`.

Follow the OS instead: `theme::follow_system_appearance(window, cx)` — call it
once per window from its root-view constructor. It applies the current OS
appearance immediately and then switches between the registered `"light"` and
`"dark"` themes whenever the desktop does; `theme::stop_following_system_appearance(cx)`
ends it and `ThemeProvider::follows_system_appearance()` reports the mode for a
three-way Light/Dark/System setting. It is opt-in, so an app that pins one
appearance keeps it.

## Theming

Every base value is transcribed verbatim from
`packages/styles/themes/default/variables.css` in `oklch()`. Derived values use
the same `color-mix(in oklab, …)` weights the stylesheet uses.

**Base:** `background`, `foreground`, `muted`, `scrollbar`, `border`,
`separator`, `focus`, `link`, `backdrop`.

**Containers:** `surface` (`.background` / `.foreground`), `surface_secondary`,
`surface_tertiary`, `overlay` (floating panels), `segment` (segmented controls).

**Roles:** `default`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` — each a
`RoleColor` with `color`, `foreground`, and derived `hover()`, `soft()`,
`soft_hover()`, `soft_foreground()`. No numbered scales in v3.

**Fields:** `field.background`, `field.foreground`, `field.placeholder`,
`field.border`, plus `field.hover()` and `field.focus()`.

**Derived on `ThemeColors`:** `background_secondary()`, `background_tertiary()`,
`background_inverse()`, `separator_secondary()`, `separator_tertiary()`,
`role(name)`.

**Layout:** `radius` (8px) with `radius_xs()`…`radius_4xl()` and `capped(r)` for v3's `min(32px, ..)` ceiling, `field_radius`,
`border_width`, `field_border_width`, `disabled_opacity`, `ring_offset_width`,
`spacing`, `surface_shadow` / `overlay_shadow` / `field_shadow` (all empty in
dark mode), `skeleton_animation`, `tooltip_delay_ms`, `tooltip_close_delay_ms`,
`cursor_interactive` (`CursorStyle::PointingHand` — v3's `cursor: pointer`; the
cursor every interactive control shows on hover).

HeroGPUI-only layout tokens (no upstream CSS variable; each defaults to the
literal it replaced, so a theme that ignores them renders v3's pixels):
`tabs_hover_opacity` (0.7 — the dim an unselected Tabs item takes on hover,
clamped to 0..=1), `tooltip_cooldown_ms` (500 — the warm window after the
pointer leaves a tooltip during which the next tip opens without its delay;
a per-tooltip close delay extends it),
`long_press_ms` (500 — how long `DropdownTrigger::LongPress` waits) and
`hover_fade_ms` (100 — the background fade duration; `0` resolves
immediately). All four plus `tooltip_delay_ms` / `tooltip_close_delay_ms` are
settable through `ThemeBuilder` and the sparse `ThemeDocument` JSON.

```rust
div().bg(cx.colors().surface.background)
div().bg(cx.colors().accent.soft())
div().text_color(cx.colors().muted)
```

Custom theme — override a base token and every derived value follows:

```rust
use gpui::px;
use herogpui::core::oklch;
use herogpui::theme::{snow, Theme};

let brand = Theme::builder("brand", Theme::dark())
    .accent(oklch(0.55, 0.23, 295.0))
    .role("success", oklch(0.73, 0.19, 150.0), snow())
    .radius(px(6.))          // field_radius follows at 1.5x
    .cursor_interactive(gpui::CursorStyle::Arrow) // every control's hover cursor
    .build();
herogpui::theme::set_theme(brand, cx);
```

The same sparse overrides as JSON, behind the `serde` feature — derived
hover / soft mixes still go through `ThemeBuilder`:

```rust
use herogpui::ThemeDocument;

let brand = ThemeDocument::theme_from_json(r#"{
    "id": "brand",
    "base": "dark",
    "accent": "oklch(0.55 0.23 295)"
}"#).unwrap();
```

Color math (`herogpui-core`): `oklch(l, c, h)`, `oklcha(..)`,
`mix_oklab(a, b, t)`, `soft_mix(color, pct)`, `with_alpha`, `readable_color`.

## Prop vocabularies

**Corner radii.** v3 names a different step per component, so `util` has one
helper each rather than a single "control" radius: `control_radius` (3xl, 24px —
button, toggle button, avatar), `soft_radius` (2xl, 16 — chip, menu and list
rows, colour area), `small_radius` (xl, 12 — close button, tag, link, tooltip),
`key_radius` (lg, 8 — `Kbd`), `hairline_radius` (sm, 4 — separator, skeleton),
`field_radius` (12 — every form field) and `container_radius` (`min(32px, 3xl)` —
cards, the table and every floating panel; Surface carries none, upstream
`.surface` declares no radius). `.shots/design_audit.py` diffs these
against the real stylesheets. An `sx` corner refines a painted part
(slider track/fill/thumb, switch track/thumb) per corner, winning over
the part's own radius only where the override names it.

**Control heights** are v3's desktop values, 32 / 36 / 40 for sm / md / lg. Its
sheet is mobile-first (`.button` is `h-10 md:h-9`), and a desktop app is past
every breakpoint. A labelled button has no minimum width: it hugs its content, as
`.button`'s `w-fit` does.

**Number formatting.** `formatOptions` is v3's `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`;
`herogpui_core::NumberFormat` implements the subset the components use —
`NumberFormat::{decimal,percent,currency("USD"),unit("kilogram")}` with
`currency_sign`, `unit_display`, `minimum_fraction_digits`,
`maximum_fraction_digits` and `use_grouping`. Taken by `Meter`, `NumberField`,
`ProgressBar`, `ProgressCircle` and `Slider`. `locale` is not offered: choosing
separators, digit systems and currency placement per locale needs CLDR *number*
data, and `herogpui-core`, where `NumberFormat` lives, carries no ICU
dependency. The date components do carry one, which is why a calendar follows
the reader's locale and a formatted number does not.

v3 replaced v2's `variant` × `color` matrix with distinct enums:

| Enum | Values | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `Variant` | `Primary` `Secondary` `Tertiary` `Outline` `Ghost` `Danger` `DangerSoft` | Button, ButtonGroup (no `Outline`) |
| `FieldVariant` | `Primary` `Secondary` | every form control |
| `Prominence` | `Transparent` `Default` `Secondary` `Tertiary` | none: Card and Surface define their own `CardVariant`/`SurfaceVariant` |
| `Backdrop` | `Opaque` `Blur` `Transparent` | Modal, Drawer, AlertDialog |
| `Color` | `Default` `Accent` `Success` `Warning` `Danger` | components with a color role |
| `Size` | `Sm` `Md` `Lg` | most components |
| `SizeXl` | `Xs` `Sm` `Md` `Lg` `Xl` | ColorSwatch, ColorSwatchPicker |
| `SelectionMode` | `None` `Single` `Multiple` | ListBox, TagGroup, ToggleButtonGroup, Dropdown, Table, Select, Autocomplete, ComboBox |
| `Placement` | `Bottom` `BottomStart` `BottomEnd` `Top` `TopStart` `TopEnd` `Left` `Right` | every floating panel: Popover, Dropdown, Select, ComboBox, Autocomplete, ColorPicker |
| `Orientation` | `Horizontal` `Vertical` | Separator, Toolbar, Slider, Tabs, ButtonGroup, ColorSlider, groups |
| `Weekday` | `Sun`...`Sat` | `firstDayOfWeek` on every date component |
| `VisibleDuration` | `Months(n)` `Weeks(n)` `Days(n)` | `visibleDuration` on Calendar, RangeCalendar |
| `PageBehavior` | `Visible` `Single` | how far navigation steps |
| `SelectionAlignment` | `Start` `Center` `End` | where the selection sits in the visible range |

`Placement` collapses v3's physical and logical spellings (`"bottom left"` and
`"bottom start"`) onto one value each, since this port has no RTL mode. Position
a panel with `util::placed_panel(placement, offset)` — or
`util::placed_field_panel` for a trigger-width one — and always hand the result
to `util::floating`, since gpui paints in tree order and `absolute` alone does
not lift a panel above later siblings.


## Render props

v3 passes values *into* a child render function. Where a monolithic builder
computes those values anyway, it hands them to a closure instead of asking the
caller to supply them — so the prop is real, just inverted:

- `Table::indicator(|SortDirection| ..)` — v3's `Table.SortableColumnHeader`
  `indicator`, handed `sortDirection`
- `Pagination::link(|page, is_active| ..)` — `Pagination.Link`, handed `isActive`
- `InputOTP::slot(|index, Option<char>| ..)` — `InputOTP.Slot`, handed `index`
- `Dropdown/Menu::item_content(|key, is_selected, is_indeterminate| ..)` —
  `Dropdown.Item`, handed `isSelected` / `isIndeterminate`
- `Slider::thumb(|index, value| ..)` — `Slider.Thumb`, handed `index`
- `TimeField::segment(|TimeSegment, text| ..)` — `TimeField.Segment`
- `DateField::segment(|FieldSegment, text| ..)` — `DateField.Segment`, covering date and optional time slots

## Controlled and uncontrolled

Every component takes the controlled prop as an `Option`, so leaving it unset
hands the state to the component, seeded from the matching `default*`:

```rust
Checkbox::new("terms").is_selected(self.agreed)    // controlled
Checkbox::new("terms").default_selected(true)      // uncontrolled

Select::new("lang", opts).is_open(self.open)       // controlled
Select::new("lang", opts).default_open(false)      // uncontrolled
Dropdown::uncontrolled(trigger, items)             // no `is_open` at all
```

The uncontrolled value lives in `Window::use_keyed_state`, keyed on the
component's id — so two uncontrolled components that share an id share their
state. `Popover`, `Accordion` and `Tooltip` therefore take an `id` purely to
tell instances apart. Pairs available: `is_selected`/`default_selected`
(Checkbox, Switch, ToggleButton), `is_open`/`default_open` (Popover, Select, ComboBox,
Autocomplete, Dropdown, DatePicker, DateRangePicker), `selected_key`/`default_selected_key`
(Tabs), `expanded_keys`/`default_expanded_keys` (Accordion),
`is_year_picker_open`/`default_year_picker_open` (Calendar, RangeCalendar),
`value`/`default_value` (RadioGroup, Select, CheckboxGroup, Slider, ColorArea,
ColorField, ColorPicker, ColorSlider, ColorSwatchPicker, Autocomplete, ComboBox,
Calendar, RangeCalendar, DatePicker, DateRangePicker, DateField, TimeField,
Input, TextField, SearchField, TextArea, NumberField),
`input_value`/`default_input_value` (ComboBox). Where the
controlled prop is itself an `Option` — `RadioGroup::value(None)` — supplying it
at all is what makes the component controlled.

For components whose value lives in a state entity, the entity constructor *is*
the uncontrolled seed: `InputState::with_value`, `NumberState::with_value`,
`CalendarState::with_selected`, `DateRangeState::with_range`,
`TimeState::with_value`.

## Validation

`validate` is a function the component runs, not something the caller
substitutes for. It returns the message to show, or `None`:

```rust
TextField::new(state)
    .validate(|v| (v.len() < 3).then(|| "At least 3 characters".into()))
    .validation_errors(["That name is taken"])   // e.g. from a server
```

`validation::resolve` fixes the precedence — the controlled `is_invalid`, then
`validationErrors`, then `validate`, with the component's own `error_message` as
the fallback rather than an addition. Available on Input, TextField, TextArea,
SearchField, NumberField, Checkbox, Switch, InputOTP, ColorField, DateField and
TimeField. `Form` takes `validation_errors(ValidationErrors)` — HeroUI's
`Record<string, string | string[]>` record of server errors keyed by field
name. The form routes each name into that field's own error slot; editing a
field clears only its messages, reset hides them all, and a genuinely new
record re-arms every named field even when the content is identical (a clone
keeps the record's identity and re-arms nothing). Identity is reference
identity, as in React Stately: retain one record for as long as the response
is current and pass a clone each frame; building a fresh record per frame —
even with identical content — is a new server response and re-arms.
Unmatched names neither display nor block; fields without an error-display
path receive no routed messages, so a name can never block invisibly.

## Accessibility

gpui reports an element to a screen reader only when it has both an `.id(..)`
and a role, so the port states each control's role explicitly. The contract is
React Aria 3.51.0's, read from its hooks: a checkbox is `CheckBox` with
tri-state checked, a switch is `Switch`, a toggle button is `Button` with a
pressed state — or `RadioButton` inside a single-selection group, as
`useToggleButtonGroupItem` swaps it — a text field takes the role of its input
type, a slider is a `Group` around one `Slider` per thumb, and a progress bar
keeps its bounds while dropping its value when indeterminate.

`a11y::Name::field` performs the join `useField` performs with ids: the label
names the control, and the description plus any validation messages become its
description, so labels and messages reach assistive technology through the
existing field plumbing rather than a second set of props. `a11y::Range`
carries a numeric control's bounds, value, step and value text, clamped once.
Nothing here is a new builder — the roles and names are derived from the props
each component already takes.

The overlays follow: a modal, drawer, popover and toast card are dialogs, a
tooltip is a `Tooltip`, a dropdown's panel is a `Menu` whose rows are menu
items, and an accordion's own trigger row reports `aria-expanded`.

The collections state their structure. A list box is a `ListBox` of
`ListBoxOption`s carrying `aria-selected`; a table is a `Grid` — a `TreeGrid`
when its rows nest — with a header row of `ColumnHeader`s, a `RowGroup` body,
and `GridCell` (or `RowHeader`) cells carrying `aria-colindex`; tabs are a
`TabList` of `Tab`s over a `TabPanel`; a toolbar is a `Toolbar`, or a `Group`
when nested inside another; breadcrumbs are a `List` of `ListItem`s holding
links; pagination is a `Navigation` of buttons; a tag group is a `Grid` of
`Row`s. Set position (`aria-posinset`/`aria-setsize`) and grid counts
(`aria-rowcount`/`aria-colcount`/`aria-rowindex`) appear exactly where React
Aria puts them — under virtualization, where the rendered rows are a window
onto a longer collection.

Select, ComboBox and Autocomplete report the parts they build: a `Button`
trigger with `aria-expanded`, a `ListBox` popup, `ListBoxOption` rows, and
`aria-activedescendant` on the highlighted row. `role="combobox"` is *not*
stated: React Aria puts it on the text input, and these components compose a
`crate::input::Input` whose role its own render decides.

gpui exposes no `aria-disabled`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`,
`aria-readonly`, `aria-controls`, `aria-roledescription`, `aria-haspopup`,
`aria-multiselectable`, `aria-sort`, `aria-current` or live-region builder, and
no id-reference graph for `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby`; those are
recorded as omissions in `crates/herogpui-components/src/a11y.rs`, and
`.shots/a11y_audit.py` is the gate. `ButtonGroup`, `InputGroup`,
`ProgressCircle`, `Fieldset`, `ToastViewport`, `ColorSwatch` and `Toolbar`
take an optional `.id()`: a named instance reports its node and an unnamed
one does not, because a constant id would fold two instances into one.
`Separator` is the remaining pending row — AccessKit 0.24 has no
`Role::Separator`.

## Component API pattern

All components are `#[derive(IntoElement)]` builders implementing `RenderOnce`:

```rust
Button::new("save")
    .child(icon)          // ordered children: leading icon first, then label text
    .child("Save")
    .variant(Variant::Primary)
    .size(Size::Md)
    .is_pending(true)
    .full_width(true)
    .on_press(cx.listener(|this, _, _, cx| this.save(cx)))
```

Every builder also carries one `sx` slot for caller-owned low-level styling
— this port's answer to React's `sx`. The closure styles a scratch `Div`
with GPUI's own `Styled` methods; the refinement it leaves behind is merged
over the component's root element at the end of render, after every value
the variant and the theme chose, so the override wins:

```rust
Button::new("save")
    .label("Save")
    .sx(|el| el.bg(gpui::rgba(0xffa500ff)).text_color(gpui::rgba(0x000000ff)))
```

State-driven layers a component draws itself — Button's hover fade, the
press-scale geometry — read the override's background and pixel size, so the
override holds across states too. Where that means a state stops moving —
an `sx` background freezes Button's hover fade on the override — the component
names the escape hatch (`Button::hover_bg`).

Controlled state lives in your entity (`InputState`, `CalendarState`,
`TimeState`, `NumberState`, `OtpState`, `DateRangeState`):

```rust
let name = cx.new(|cx| InputState::new(cx));
TextField::new(name.clone()).label("Name").is_required(true)
```

Callbacks: `Fn(&ClickEvent/&str/f32/usize/bool/Option<Date>, &mut Window, &mut App)`.
Fields cloned into closures must be `Arc`.

## Components (67)

HeroUI documents 71 components; this file groups them into 67 entries — a few
entries cover a component together with its group or slot siblings, and two
entries (`PickerColor`, `DateConstraints`) describe shared helpers. The gallery
and website group the same components into 66 pages.

v3 keeps `size` on nineteen components (Button, ButtonGroup, ToggleButton*,
Chip, TagGroup, Badge, Avatar, Switch, Meter, ProgressBar, ProgressCircle,
Spinner, Pagination, Modal, AlertDialog, ScrollShadow, ColorSwatch*) and gives
every form field one height instead — `util::FIELD_HEIGHT` / `FIELD_TEXT` /
`FIELD_ICON`. `color` survives only on Avatar, Badge, Chip, ColorSwatch*, Meter,
ProgressBar, ProgressCircle, Spinner and Typography; elsewhere `variant` (or
`status`, on Alert) is the whole visual vocabulary. `CloseButton` has neither.

### Buttons
- **Button** — `variant(Variant)`, `size`, `full_width`, `is_icon_only`, `radius(px)`, `is_disabled`, `is_pending`, ordered children (the icons and label text are children in order, matching v3 — there are no start/end content slots), `on_press`
  - `hover_bg(Hsla)` names the fill the hover fade eases *to*. v3 has no such prop — on the web it is `className="hover:bg-…"` — and it exists because an `sx` background alone pins both of the fade's endpoints (a fade back to the variant colour would paint over the override), leaving a custom surface with no hover. With it the fade runs from the resting background (the `sx` one when set, the variant's otherwise) to the named colour, on the same timing; the press state is the usual opacity step either way.
- **ButtonGroup** — `id()`, `variant`, `size`, `orientation`, `button(Button)` (members inherit), `is_disabled`, `full_width`. A named group reports `role="group"`.
- **CloseButton** — `is_disabled`, `icon(el)`, `content(|state| el)`, `on_press`, `hover_bg(color)` (v3's `variant` has one value, so there is nothing to select and no builder for it). `hover_bg` is additive, matching `Button::hover_bg`: the fade rests on the `sx` background when set, else `--default`, and eases to the named colour.
- **ToggleButton / ToggleButtonGroup** — `is_selected`, `variant(ToggleVariant::{Default,Ghost})`, `size`, `hover_bg(color)`, `radius(px)`, `selection_mode`, `is_detached`, `orientation`, `full_width`, `ToggleSeparator`. Both apply v3's `scale(0.97)` press. `hover_bg` follows the same resting-endpoint contract as `Button::hover_bg`; `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius` and a group edge still rounds only the member's outer corners.
  - `ToggleButton::on_change(&bool)` reports the selection a press moves to, alongside `on_press`. A button's selection key is `key()` when given, otherwise its element id, so a group can namespace child ids without breaking selection.

### Collections
- **Dropdown** — `Dropdown::new(trigger, items, is_open).placement(Placement).on_open_change(&bool).on_action(&str).row_hover_bg(color).radius(px)`, `MenuItem::new(key,label).shortcut().icon().danger()`, `MenuItem::SectionLabel`, `MenuItem::Separator`. Built-in labels use 14px/20px medium text, descriptions and section headers use 12px/16px, and shortcut hints render as light `Kbd`. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, and the menu panel's entry zoom interpolates the override; an item's own `rounded-2xl` mark is an inner part and keeps its step.
  The menu positions against the measured trigger: all eight placements flip
  to the side with more room when the preferred side cannot fit, keep a 12px
  cross-axis viewport inset, and cap the scroller to the available height with
  short menus keeping their natural height.
  Submenus position independently against their row end top and flip sides to
  the side with more room when needed; the parent stays anchored and outside
  presses still dismiss the whole menu.
  Descriptions wrap within the popover width; long menus remain scrollable.
  - selection: `selection_mode(SelectionMode)`, `selected_keys`, `disabled_keys`, `on_selection_change(&[SharedString])`, `on_action(&str)`. Selected items draw a check; disabled ones are muted and inert. The next selection comes from `selection::next_selection`, shared with ToggleButtonGroup and Table.
- **ListBox** — `ListBox::new(id, items).selection_mode().selected_keys().disabled_keys().escape_key_behavior(EscapeKeyBehavior::{ClearSelection,None}).max_h().row_hover_bg(color).on_selection_change().on_action()`, `ListBoxItem::new(key,label).description().icon().shortcut().danger()`, `::section()`, `::separator()`. Built-in labels use 14px/20px medium text, descriptions and section headers use 12px/16px, and shortcut hints render as light `Kbd`. Fixed-row virtual lists cap at `max_h`, shrink below it in a bounded parent, and page by the visible viewport, including after resize, while skipping disabled stops.
- **TagGroup** — `TagGroup::new(id, tags).full_width(bool).label().selection_mode().selected_keys().escape_key_behavior(EscapeKeyBehavior::{ClearSelection,None}).size().variant(TagVariant::{Default,Surface}).hover_bg(color).remove_hover_bg(color).empty_state().on_remove().on_selection_change()`, `Tag::new(key,label).icon().remove_content(render)`
  Small/medium tags set 12px text with 16px leading; large tags set 14px text
  with 20px leading. Labels, descriptions, and empty states also set their own
  line height, so inherited leading does not change tag heights.

### Colors
ColorSlider labels/output, ColorPicker triggers, and ColorField display text use 14px text with a 20px line height independent of their parent.
- **PickerColor** — shared value: `from_hex`, `to_hex`, `from_rgb`, `to_rgb`, `to_hsla`, `channel()`, `with_channel()`, `with_alpha()`
- **ColorArea** — `ColorArea::new(id, value)`; `color_space(ColorSpace)` sets both axes to that space's channel pair, `x_channel` / `y_channel` override either, `size(w,h)`, `show_dots` (the dot-grid overlay), `is_disabled`, `on_change`, `on_change_end`
- **ColorField** — `ColorField::new(id, value)`; `channel(ColorChannel)`, `color_space(ColorSpace)`, `label`, `description`, `variant`, `full_width`, `radius(px)`, the validity flags. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and both of its boxes follow it: the static display box sets the resolved value back over the shared field chrome, and the editable path forwards it to the inner `Input` it renders.
  - `full_width(true)` expands both the outer wrapper and control to the available parent width.
  - `state(Entity<InputState>)` makes it **editable**; without one it is a read-only display of `value`. `placeholder`, and `on_change(&Option<PickerColor>)` reporting `None` when the text is not a colour, exactly as v3 types it. With a `channel` the text is that channel's number rather than a hex value.
- **ColorPicker** — `label`, `is_open`, `show_alpha`, `font_family(name)`, `on_change`, `on_open_change`
  - When the preferred side cannot fit the popup, it flips to the side with more room, keeping a 12px cross-axis viewport inset and an 8px trigger gap, and its scroller caps to the available height so taller control stacks scroll vertically; Tab moves through area/hue/alpha and reveals each focused control.
- **ColorSlider** — `ColorSlider::new(id, value, channel).color_space(ColorSpace).orientation().length().show_label().on_change().on_change_end()`
  - `color_space` is not cosmetic: HSL and HSB saturation are different quantities for the same colour, so a saturation slider reads and writes through `PickerColor::{channel_in, with_channel_in}`. Every other channel is space-independent.
- **ColorSwatch** — `ColorSwatch::new(color)`, `id()`, `size(SizeXl)`, `shape(SwatchShape::{Circle,Square})`. A named swatch reports `role="img"` named by the hex; v3's `colorName` is that accessible name.
- **ColorSwatchPicker** — `value`, `size`, `shape`, `layout(SwatchLayout::{Grid,Stack})`, `on_change`

### Controls
- **Slider** — `Slider::new(id, value).value().default_value().min_value().max_value().step().orientation().size(SliderSize).label().show_value().format_options().on_change(&f32).on_change_end(&f32)`. The multi-thumb form is `values(Vec<f32>)` + `on_change_all(&[f32])`; dragging moves whichever thumb is nearest, and `thumb(|index, value|)` is v3's `Slider.Thumb` render prop. `size(SliderSize)` is additive, not a v3 prop: `Md` (the default) is v3's geometry — a 20px rail, a 28x20-around-24x16 two-layer thumb and a 12px axis inset — while `Sm` is a 6px pill rail with an 8px inset and a single 12px round knob in the foreground colour. Labels and outputs use 14px text with a fixed 20px line height.
- **Switch** — `is_selected`, `size`, `hover_bg(color)`, `is_disabled`, `is_read_only`, `is_invalid`, `is_required`, `label(el)`, `on_change(&bool)` / `on_press`. v3's `value` is the form-submission value, not the state, so there is no builder for it. Content uses 14px text with 20px lines; the built-in label uses 16px text with 24px lines.

### Data Display
- **Badge** — `BadgeAnchor::new()` is v3's `Badge.Anchor`, the positioning wrapper whose children are the anchored element plus the `Badge::new().variant(BadgeVariant::{Primary,Secondary,Soft}).color().size().text_size(px).placement(BadgePlacement)` composed as a later child. `BadgeLabel::new()` is the `px-0.5` text slot — v3 auto-wraps plain text children in it, which GPUI cannot intercept, so the wrap is explicit. No children on the badge is v3's dot badge, and the page-background ring stays unconditional.
- **Chip** — `Chip::new().variant(ChipVariant::{Primary,Secondary,Tertiary,Soft}).color().size().text_size(px)` renders arbitrary ordered children verbatim (an icon, a dot, a `ChipLabel`, a trailing element); `ChipLabel::new()` is the `px-0.5` text slot for the label text. A removable chip is `TagGroup`, which is where v3 puts `onRemove`.
- **Table** — `Table::new(columns).row(cells).variant(TableVariant::{Primary,Secondary}).row_hover_bg(color).radius(px).on_row_click(&usize, &ClickEvent)` — `variant` is the whole visual story in v3; `isStriped`/`isBordered` were v2. Headers use 12px/16px text; body cells use 14px/20px text in ordinary and virtual rows. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, replacing the wrapper shell's default; the `Primary` tray paints its own radius over that shell exactly as it covers the default, so the override shows where the default does (`Secondary`).
  - Horizontal wheel input scrolls columns; vertical input does not shift them sideways.
  - columns: `column(TableColumn::new("Name").allows_sorting(true).is_row_header(true))`. `is_row_header` has no a11y layer to reach, so it renders that column's cells in medium weight.
  - selection: `selection_mode`, `selected_keys`, `on_selection_change(&[SharedString])`, `keyed_row(key, cells)` (a row's key defaults to its index). Adds a checkbox column, with select-all in the header for `Multiple`.
  - sorting: `sort_descriptor(SortDescriptor::new(col, SortDirection::Ascending))`, `on_sort_change`, `show_indicator`. `SortDescriptor::next` gives the descriptor a header click should produce — flip the sorted column, start any other ascending. **The table never reorders its own rows**: a row is already-rendered cells, so the caller sorts its data and rebuilds.
  - keyboard: PageUp moves from the body to the first column header — from the top of a virtual body; mid-body it pages by the visible viewport. Enter/Space sorts a sortable header; Down/PageDown returns to the first/last enabled row. Unsortable headers remain outside the Tab order and preserve their configured column widths.
  - virtualization: with `row_height` + `virtual_rows`, the fixed-row body caps at `max_h`, shrinks below it in a bounded parent, and PageUp/PageDown move by the visible viewport, including after resize, while skipping disabled stops.
  - resizing: `TableColumn::allows_resizing(true).default_width(px(..)).min_width(px(..)).max_width(px(..))`; use `width(px(..))` plus `Table::on_resize` for controlled widths. `on_resize_start` / `on_resize` / `on_resize_end` receive the known `(column label, pixel width)` map for pointer and keyboard resizing.
  - `empty_state(el)` for `renderEmptyState`; `is_pending(bool)` + `on_load_more(fn)` for the scroll-intersection load-more sentinel.

### Date and Time
- **DateConstraints** — shared by all five: `min_value`, `max_value`, `is_date_unavailable(fn)`, `first_day_of_week(Weekday)`, `weeks_in_month`. Each component takes them individually, or a whole set via `.constraints(..)`. The default first weekday comes from the operating system's regional date preferences and ICU4X's compiled CLDR week data; invalid or unavailable preferences fall back to Sunday, and `first_day_of_week` remains an explicit override. The month grid's own text follows the same preference: the month and weekday names, and the order of the year-and-month heading, come from ICU4X's compiled CLDR (a Japanese reader gets a year-first heading, not a translated template), falling back to English when CLDR does not know the reported locale. On `wasm32-unknown-unknown` there is no operating system to ask -- the browser exposes no locale to `locale_config` -- so a calendar compiled for the web always draws that English fallback, whatever the visitor's browser language.
- **Calendar** — `CalendarState::new(cx)`, `Calendar::new(state).value(..).is_disabled().is_read_only().is_invalid().day_hover_bg(color).nav_hover_bg(color).year_hover_bg(color).focused_value().on_focus_change().on_change(&Option<Date>)` plus the constraints. The `locale(tag)` Unicode calendar extension selects the grid system; month/year navigation, bounds and alignment use that system, while values and callbacks stay Gregorian.
- **DateField** — three editable date segments in the operating system's regional order and separators, plus optional time segments in the regional order, separators, padding, and localized day-period names, with click-to-focus, arrow steppers that roll over month and year correctly, and the `segment(|FieldSegment, text|)` render prop. `locale(tag)` overrides that regional format (v3's `I18nProvider`). The ISO text stays in the bound `InputState`, so `name`, `FormField::text` and `on_change` are unchanged. `DateField::new(InputState).locale().label().full_width().is_required().is_invalid().font_family(name).variant().placeholder_value().should_force_leading_zeros(true).radius(px).value(Option<Date>).on_change(&Option<Date>)`; month, day and hour padding can be forced to two digits. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: the resolved value goes back over the shared field chrome, which paints the default, and the segments' own `rounded-md` marks stay.
  - Group text and text slots use 14px text with a 20px line height, independent of parent leading.
  - constraints: `min_value`, `max_value`, `is_date_unavailable`, or `constraints(DateConstraints)`. The three ways a typed date can be wrong — unparseable, out of range, unavailable — report as distinct messages, and `on_change` yields `None` for a date the constraints reject, so a caller never receives a value it said it would not accept.
- **DatePicker** — `DatePicker::new(CalendarState).label().locale().is_open().on_open_change().value().is_disabled().is_invalid().on_change()` plus the constraints; `locale` is forwarded to the embedded field and the popover calendar. State and form data remain ISO-formatted.
- **DateRangePicker** — `DateRangeState::new(cx)`, `DateRangePicker::new(state).label().placeholder().size().is_open().is_disabled().trigger_hover_bg(color).is_invalid().on_open_change(&bool).on_change()`, plus the `DateConstraints` setters; both embedded date fields use the operating system's regional date format while state and form data remain ISO-formatted
  - the popover renders `RangeCalendar`, so the hover preview between the anchor and the cursor, the constraint treatments and the year picker all come along.
- **RangeCalendar** — `RangeCalendar::new(DateRangeState).value(start, end).allows_non_contiguous_ranges().day_hover_bg(color).nav_hover_bg(color).year_hover_bg(color).focused_value().on_focus_change().on_change(start, end)` plus the constraints. During a contiguous selection, `is_date_unavailable` receives the first endpoint and derives temporary cell, focus and navigation bounds by scanning through one visible duration on each side plus the sentinel day beyond each limit; non-contiguous mode removes those interior bounds while unavailable endpoints remain inert. `locale(tag)` uses the same calendar-system conversions for the grid, paging, year picker and unavailable-range scan. Day buttons use 14px/20px medium text in all states; custom `cell` content inherits these metrics.
- **TimeField** — `TimeState::with_value(cx, Time::new(9,30))`, `TimeField::new(state).value().min_value().max_value().placeholder_value().hour_cycle(HourCycle::{H12,H24}).should_force_leading_zeros(true).show_seconds().stepper_hover_bg(color).font_family(name).radius(px).on_change(&Option<Time>)`; without explicit overrides, `TimeField` and time-granularity `DateField` use the system regional segment order, literals, numeric padding, localized day-period names, and 12/24-hour cycle, while an empty time starts at midnight. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: the resolved value goes back over the shared field chrome, which paints the default, while the segments keep their own `rounded-md` and the steppers their fixed 4px corners.
  - Group text and text slots use 14px text with a 20px line height, independent of parent leading.
  - `full_width(true)` expands both the outer wrapper and control to the available parent width.

### Feedback
- **Alert** — `Alert::new(title).description().status(Color).radius(px)` plus composed children (v3 spells it `status`, removed `variant`/`radius`, and removed `isClosable`/`onClose` — a close affordance is an ordinary child, e.g. a composed `CloseButton`). `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and it replaces the root's default `--radius-3xl` (capped).
- **Meter** — `Meter::new(id, value).value().min_value().max_value().value_label().label().show_value().color().size().radius(px)`. Labels and outputs use 14px text with a fixed 20px line height. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, forwarded to the bar the meter delegates its track to — the same ride-along as the `sx` slot — so it replaces that bar's size-step radius.
- **ProgressBar** — `ProgressBar::new(id)`, then `value`, `min_value`, `max_value`, `value_label`, `is_indeterminate`, `size`, `color`, `radius(px)`, `label`, `show_value_label`, `format_options(NumberFormat)`. Labels and outputs use 14px text with a fixed 20px line height. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`: the size still picks the default, and the override replaces it for the track and every fill segment inside it.
- **ProgressCircle** — `id()`, `value`, `min_value`, `max_value`, `is_indeterminate`, `color`, `size(Size)` (32/48/64px), `show_value_label`. A named ring reports `role="progressbar"`. The ring weight is 10% of the diameter, as v3 scales it with `size`.
- **Skeleton** — `id`, `w`, `h`, `radius(px)`, `animation_type(SkeletonAnimation::{Shimmer,Pulse,None})` (defaults to `--skeleton-animation`). v3 renders the skeleton *or* the content, so there is no `isLoaded`. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, replacing the near-square `rounded-sm` default.
- **Spinner** — `size(SpinnerSize::{Sm,Md,Lg,Xl})`, `color`, `current_color(Hsla)` for `color="current"` (gpui svgs do not inherit text colour). The diameter does not shrink in flex layouts; the app reduced-motion preference stops rotation.

### Calendar view model (`calendar_view`)

`Calendar` and `RangeCalendar` show a month grid, several month grids side by
side, a run of week rows, or a rolling window of days. Day cells, month headings and
year cells use 14px/20px medium text; weekday labels use 12px/16px medium text.
Headers have 16px bottom padding, weekday labels have 8px bottom padding, and
date rows start 4px below the weekday block. Calendar rows are contiguous;
RangeCalendar retains 2px vertical cell margins.
Calendar single-month, week and day rows use seven 36px columns without horizontal gaps, aligned
with their weekday headings.
Multiple-month views use 256px panels separated by 32px, with square cells one
seventh of the panel width and horizontal scrolling when the host is narrower.
Day views retain seven weekday columns, render dates before the requested start
as disabled, and leave blank cells after its end. Navigation still uses the
requested day count.
The year picker overlays the retained day area without changing the view dimensions.
Its year list scrolls independently and reveals the active row on opening, keyboard
navigation, or a date-bound change that moves that year to another row.

- `visible_duration(VisibleDuration::Months(2) | Weeks(2) | Days(5))`
- `page_behavior(PageBehavior::Visible | Single)` — step the whole range or one unit
- `selection_alignment(SelectionAlignment::Start | Center | End)` — applied until
  the user navigates or picks, after which the state pins the displayed range.
  Picking from an initially aligned view preserves its month/week/day anchor.
  `Center` matches React Aria: it halves the duration and then backs off again on
  an even count, so a 2-up range aligns like `Start`.
- `is_year_picker_open(bool)` + `on_year_picker_open_change(fn)` — supplying the
  handler is what turns the heading into the trigger, so the affordance never
  appears without something behind it.

The geometry is pure and testable: `calendar_view::{page, aligned_anchor,
week_start, month_headings, linear_cells, range_heading, year_page}`.

### Forms
- **Input** — `InputState {value,cursor,anchor,focus_handle}`, `variant(FieldVariant)`, `label`, `placeholder`, `description`, `error_message`, `start/end_content`, `full_width`, `is_clearable`, `clear_hover_bg(color)`, `is_required`, `is_disabled`, `is_read_only`, `is_invalid`, `on_change(&str)`, `on_submit(&str)`. Text adornments inherit the field's 14px text and 20px line height. Labels use 14px/20px and descriptions/errors use 12px/16px, independent of host leading. Platform text replacement, composition updates, and paste preserve selection, filtering, and change callbacks. Enter during composition does not submit the field.
  - `input_type(InputType::{Text,Password,Email,Number,Tel,Url,Search})` — `Password` masks, `Number` filters keystrokes
  - `max_length` (enforced while typing), `min_length`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `pattern(fn)`
  - `validity(&str) -> InputValidity` — a pure query; feed the result back through `is_invalid` / `error_message`
  - `height(px)` — replaces the 36px box height. Only the row height changes: the text keeps its 14px size and 20px line and stays centred. The multi-line surface (`TextArea`) ignores it — its height is content-driven with a `rows` floor.
  - `padding_x(px)` — replaces the box's 12px (`px-3`) horizontal padding. Inside an `InputGroup` the group owns the padding, so it is ignored there.
  - `is_bare(bool)` — renders the box with no background, border, field shadow or focus/invalid ring: the same chrome-less treatment `InputGroup.Input` already gets, for a field the caller paints around. Focus, editing and the invalid state itself are unchanged.
  - `font_family(name)` — the family the value, placeholder and caret measurement use (a monospace token field). The field's own text layout captures the font during `render`, before any element's text style is pushed, so the family is threaded into that captured font as well as set on the box.
  - `radius(px)` — replaces the box's corner radius. Not a v3 prop; it is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, and the resolved value is set back over the shared field chrome, which paints the default after the field's own chain. A bare or grouped box paints no chrome, so the chain already carries it.
  - The same `height(px)`, `padding_x(px)` and `is_bare(bool)` builders now reach the rest of the single-line family: `SearchField`, `NumberField`, `TimeField`, `DateField` and `ColorField` (both its static display box and the editable path, which forwards them to the inner `Input`). Each defaults to the stock 36px box, `px-3` inset and full chrome; a bare field keeps its geometry, editing and focus, and drops only the paint.
- **TextField** — the labelled wrapper around `Input`; forwards `start_content`, `height`, `padding_x`, `is_bare` and `font_family`
- **TextArea** — genuinely multi-line: one wrapping paragraph per newline, Enter inserts a newline, and the caret sits in the line it belongs to. Platform composition and paste use the shared Input handler; Enter confirms active composition before inserting a newline. Label/helper/error typography follows the shared Input wrapper (14px/20px labels; 12px/16px helper and error text). gpui wraps text by default (`WhiteSpace::Normal`); it is the single-line field that opts out with `whitespace_nowrap`. `rows`, `variant`, `full_width`, `max_length`, `min_length`, the validation flags, `on_change`, plus `padding_x`, `is_bare` and `font_family` forwarded to the inner field (`height` is not: the box grows with its content from the `rows` floor)
- **SearchField** — Input with a magnifier and clear action; labels use 14px/20px and helper/error text uses 12px/16px via the shared Input wrapper. `on_clear`, `is_required`, `is_read_only`, `is_invalid`
- **NumberField** — `format_options(NumberFormat)`, `NumberState {value,min,max,step,input}`, `hide_steppers`, `on_change(&f64)`
  - Group text and text slots use 14px text with a 20px line height, independent of parent leading.
- **InputOTP** — `OtpState::with_length(cx, n)`, `separator`, `slot_hover_bg(color)`, `radius(px)`, `on_complete(&str)`. Custom slot content inherits 14px/20px text; the built-in digits use 18px/24px text. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and every slot in the row takes it in place of the field radius; the caret and the group separator keep their own smaller radius.
- **InputGroup** — `id()`, `variant`, `label`, `description`, `error_message` + children; `InputAddon::new("$")`. A named group reports `role="group"`. Prefix and suffix text uses 14px text with 20px lines alongside the input. `height(px)` replaces the 36px single-line group box and follows through to the held field (a textarea group stays content-sized), `padding_x(px)` replaces the held field's `px-3` on sides without an addon, `font_family(name)` threads a family through to the held field's shaping and caret measurement, `radius(px)` replaces the group box's corner in place of the field radius — the resolved value goes back over the shared field chrome, which paints the default — and rides along to the held field the same way `font_family` does, so the box and the field it holds keep one corner, and `is_bare(true)` drops the group's background, border, shadow, focus ring and hover fill while keeping the field editable. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop.
- **Checkbox** — `is_selected`, `is_indeterminate`, `hover_bg(color)`, `size(CheckboxSize::{Sm,Md})`, `is_disabled`, `is_read_only`, `is_required`, `is_invalid`, `variant(FieldVariant)`, `label(el)`, `on_change(&bool)`. `size` is additive, not a v3 prop: `Md` is the pinned 16px control / 12px indicator / 14px label; `Sm` is a 14px control with a 10px indicator and 12px label text. Label content uses 14px medium text with 20px lines, independent of surrounding line height. Toggling animates: the accent fill scales and fades in while the check stroke draws (fill 100/200ms, draw 150ms after 15ms, undraw 200ms), a mid-flight reversal resumes from the rendered frame, and reduced motion snaps. A caller-drawn `indicator` replaces the stroke but keeps the fill motion.
- **CheckboxGroup** — `CheckboxGroup::new(id, options).label().value(keys).orientation().variant().is_read_only().error_message().on_change(HashSet)`, `CheckboxOption::new(key,label).description()`. Option labels use 14px/20px medium text; descriptions use 12px/16px regular text.
- **RadioGroup** — `RadioGroup::new(id, options).value().default_value().orientation().size(RadioSize::{Sm,Md}).full_width(bool).on_change(&SharedString)`. `size` is additive, not a v3 prop: `Md` is the pinned 16px control / 6px dot / 14px label; `Sm` is 14/5/12 with a 10px row gap. Option content uses 14px medium text with 20px lines, independent of surrounding line height.
- **Form** — `Form::new().field(FormField::text(state).is_required(true)).on_submit(&FormData).on_invalid(&FormData).on_reset()`, plus `submit_handler()` / `reset_handler()` to wire to buttons. v3's `name` rides on the field: the entity-backed ones (`Input`, `TextField`, `SearchField`, `TextArea`, `NumberField`) store it on their state and `FormField::text`/`number` read it back; the prop-based ones (`Checkbox`, `Switch`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Select`, `Slider`, `ColorSlider`, `ColorField`, `InputOTP`, `Autocomplete`, `DatePicker`, `TimeField`) expose `form_field()`, which borrows, so the control is still yours to place. `DateRangePicker` has `start_name`/`end_name` and `form_fields()`. `validationBehavior` travels the same way: `Allow` shows a field's message without blocking submission. `FormData::text(name)` reads a submission. The HTTP half — `action`/`method`/`encType`/`target` — has no browser to post to.
- **Label / Description / ErrorMessage / FieldError / Fieldset** — the composition slots; `Label::new(t).is_required().is_disabled().is_invalid()`, `FieldError::new().message(t)`, `Fieldset::new().id()` + `FieldsetLegend` / `FieldGroup` / `FieldsetActions`. A named fieldset reports `role="group"`.

### Layout
- **Card** — `variant(CardVariant::{Transparent,Default,Secondary,Tertiary})`, `w`, `radius(px)`, parts `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardContent`, `CardFooter`. The card itself is the padded box (`gap-3 p-4` and the capped container radius) and its parts carry none of their own: the header is a plain column, the title is `text-sm` medium on the foreground, the description `text-sm` muted, the content a `gap-1` column — its upstream `flex-1` is dropped, because the pinned-geometry test in `tests/card_deep.rs` measures the card as an auto-height column hugging its parts, which flex-1 regresses — and the footer a centered row. `transparent` paints nothing: no border, background or shadow. v3's Card is presentational: `isPressable`/`isHoverable`/`isBlurred` were v2, and an interactive card composes a `Button`.
- **Separator** — `id()`, `orientation`, `variant(SeparatorVariant::{Default,Secondary,Tertiary})`, `mx`/`my`. The weight is `--border-width`; v3 has no per-instance override. AccessKit 0.24 has no separator role, so a named instance still produces no node.
- **Surface** — `variant(SurfaceVariant::{Transparent,Default,Secondary,Tertiary})`. The v3 component is a strict root — `relative text-foreground` plus each variant's background and foreground pair — with zero default padding and gap, and no radius or border; `transparent` is just a transparent background (the outlined look in the docs examples comes from their own `className`). `padding`/`gap` are port conveniences, not v3 props: they stand in for the `flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-3xl p-6` skeleton every docs example adds through `className`. v3 also publishes its variant through `SurfaceContext` so children can read it; GPUI has no ancestor context propagation, so nothing downstream reads the surrounding surface here.
- **Toolbar** — `orientation`, `is_attached`, `gap`, `full_width(bool)`, `separator()`. Set the orientation before appending a separator; the bar creates a centred divider half its cross size.

### Media
- **Avatar** — `Avatar::new(id).name().src(ImageSource).custom_source_key(key).size().radius(px).color().variant(AvatarVariant::{Default,Soft})`, plus `on_error(f)` / `on_load(f)` for `Avatar.Image.onError`/`onLoad` (fired once per instance, no event payload), `delay_ms(ms)` for `Avatar.Fallback.delayMs` (measured from mount), `fallback(el)` for `Avatar.Fallback` children (an icon, a `+N` counter, custom text) and `fallback_color(Color)` for `Avatar.Fallback.color` — its own documented prop that overrides the parent color for everything the fallback paints. The constructor id is not a v3 prop: the image lifecycle (delay window and once-only callbacks) is keyed per instance under it, and it is required at construction so repeated avatars cannot silently merge into one instance. A changed source resets that lifecycle, so callbacks refire for the new source; a gpui `ImageSource::Custom` loader has no value identity, so omitting `custom_source_key` keeps its lifecycle stable when the closure is rebuilt inline per frame. Set `custom_source_key(key)` to identify a changed logical custom image and reset its load/error latches without using closure pointer identity. `Avatar::initials(name)` renders the default two-letter initials. Fallback text uses 14px/20px for small and medium avatars and 16px/24px for large avatars. A plain string `src` loads through gpui's asset system; a gpui `ImageSource::Custom` loader is the custom-image-component seam. Loaded images carry the same radius as the Avatar root so WebGPU and native renderers keep them inside its boundary. v3 has no AvatarGroup — its Avatar Group example is plain `Avatar` composition (`-space-x-2` overlap, `ring-2 ring-background`, an explicit +N fallback avatar).

### Navigation
- **Accordion** — `Accordion::new(items).expanded_keys(HashSet).variant(AccordionVariant::{Default,Surface}).hover_bg(color).hide_separator().on_toggle(&SharedString)`, `AccordionItem::new(key,title).subtitle().content(el)`; title, subtitle and body line heights are 20px, 16px and 20px independently of host leading, with no extra top inset above the body.
- **Breadcrumbs** — `Breadcrumbs::new(vec![Crumb::new("Home").href("#")]).id().separator(BreadcrumbSeparator::{Slash,Chevron,Dash}).separator_render(|i| custom node).full_width(bool).is_disabled(bool).on_navigate(|i, crumb, ev|)`; the last crumb is the current page — link-coloured, inert, no tab stop — even if it carries an `href`. Every link crumb is a tab stop and Enter/Space activates it.
- **Disclosure / DisclosureGroup** — `Disclosure::new(id,title).is_expanded().on_expanded_change(&bool).content(|state: DisclosureRenderState| ..)`, `DisclosureGroup::new(id).item(key,title,content).expanded_keys().on_expanded_change()`
- **Link** — `Link::new(id).label().href().icon(el).icon_first(bool).auto_focus().is_disabled().on_press()` plus `render(|state| el)` — v3's render function receives the link's interactive state (`isHovered`/`isPressed`/`isFocused`/`isFocusVisible`/`isDisabled`); the root keeps the `href`, `onPress`, focus and disabled wiring, and GPUI has no DOM props to spread. `.link` is `font-medium text-link no-underline decoration-[1.5px]` — the stylesheet is the contract, not the docs' `font-semibold` Global CSS snippet — and hover/press only recolour the decoration (`muted/50` → `muted`), never the text. Opening goes through the OS handler, so v3's `target` / `rel` / `download` have no meaning and are not offered.
- **Pagination** — `Pagination::new(id, page, total).size().full_width(bool).hover_bg(color).on_change(&usize)` — the override feeds hover and pressed together; summary, link and navigation text use size-specific 12/16, 14/20 and 16/24 font/line-height pairs independently of host leading.
- **Tabs** — `Tabs::new(id, items, selected_key).variant(TabsVariant::{Primary,Secondary}).orientation().size(TabsSize::{Sm,Md}) .full_width(bool).selected_key().default_selected_key().on_selection_change()`, `TabItem::new(key,label).content(el)`; `full_width(true)` is v3's `<Tabs.List className="w-full">` with `<Tabs.Trigger className="flex-1">` — the horizontal list fills its parent and the tabs take equal shares of it instead of hugging their labels (ignored when vertical, where tabs already stretch); both tab variants use 14px labels with a 20px line height independently of host leading.
  - Wheel input scrolls the tab list only along its configured orientation.

### Overlays

Modal, Drawer, and AlertDialog cover the window even inside clipped or positioned containers. They paint above later page content and block pointer input to the page beneath.

- **AlertDialog** — `AlertDialog::new(title).id().description().is_open().size(AlertDialogSize::{Xs,Sm,Md,Lg,Cover}).backdrop(Backdrop).placement(ModalPlacement).status(Color).is_dismissible(bool).is_keyboard_dismiss_disabled(bool).confirm_label().cancel_label().on_confirm().on_cancel().on_open_change(&bool)` plus composed children; `.child(AlertDialogCloseTrigger::new())` composes v3's `AlertDialog.CloseTrigger` X and `.footer_child(Button)` composes the caller-owned footer
  The description wraps inside the body; overflowing body content scrolls within the panel.
  - every close path — the composed X, the backdrop and Escape — reports through `on_open_change(false)` first; the built-in confirm/cancel stand-in reports through it too, then fires the consumer action. Escape and the backdrop are plain closes and never call `on_cancel`.
  - a composed footer retires the built-in pair: the caller's own `Button`s own their close wiring and the danger/pending spellings (`variant(Variant::Danger)`, `is_pending(true)`), the way v3 composes `slot="close"` buttons.
  - `is_dismissible` and `is_keyboard_dismiss_disabled` default to v3's values (backdrop dismissal off, Escape off), so opting in is explicit. `status` renders the alert glyph in that role's colour and only when set.
  - placement is anchored like Modal's, but v3's ±4px enter slide for top/bottom/auto is not ported — the fade and the zoom are.
- **Drawer** — `placement(DrawerPlacement)`, `size(px)`, `title`, `backdrop(Backdrop)`, `is_dismissible`, `is_keyboard_dismiss_disabled`, `footer_child`, `on_close`, `on_open_change(&bool)`; `.child(DrawerCloseTrigger::new())` composes v3's `Drawer.CloseTrigger` X
- **Modal** — `is_open`, `title`, `size(ModalSize::{Xs,Sm,Md,Lg,Cover,Full})`, `backdrop(Backdrop)`, `placement(ModalPlacement::{Auto,Center,Top,Bottom})`, `scroll(ModalScroll::{Inside,Outside})`, `radius(px)`, `is_dismissible`, `is_keyboard_dismiss_disabled`, `footer_child`, `on_close`, `on_open_change(&bool)`; `.child(ModalCloseTrigger::new())` composes v3's `Modal.CloseTrigger` X — the part draws only where composed, like v3
  - `Inside` scrolling retains a 40px outer margin, including with long content; `Full` fills the viewport. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`; it replaces the default panel radius but `Full` paints no radius either way, so its zoom stays a plain fade.
  - every dismissal path reports through **both** `on_close` and `on_open_change(false)`, so either callback alone is sufficient.
  - Escape closes it unless `is_keyboard_dismiss_disabled`. The overlay takes a focus handle and claims focus while nothing inside holds it; keys bubble from the focused descendant, so a text field inside keeps working. Drawer and AlertDialog behave the same way (AlertDialog defaults keyboard dismissal *off*, as v3 does).
- **Popover** — `Popover::new(trigger).is_open().placement(Placement).offset(px).should_flip(bool).padding(px).radius(px).title().show_close_button().on_open_change(&bool)`; panel text defaults to 14px with a 20px line height independently of host leading; `.child(PopoverArrow::new())` composes v3's `Popover.Arrow` part — the built-in 12px curve, or a custom child element at the resolved position but without the rotation (upstream rotates it through its `data-slot` placement CSS; The pinned GPUI transforms only `svg()` elements at construction). `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, and the panel's entry zoom interpolates the override, so the animation never parts company with the painted shape.
  - `should_flip` routes through gpui's `anchored().snap_to_window()`, which slides the panel back inside the viewport rather than mirroring it to the opposite side.
- **Toast** — `Toast::new(title).description().variant(Color).closable().close_hover_bg(color).padding(px).radius(px).push(duration, cx)`; `ToastViewport::new().id().placement(ToastPlacement).gap().max_visible_toasts().width()` is `Toast.Provider` and a named viewport reports `role="region"`; `toast_store(cx)` global. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, and the card's entry zoom interpolates the override, so the animation never parts company with the painted shape; the close button inside the card keeps its own smaller radius.
- **Tooltip** — `Tooltip::new("tip").placement(TooltipPlacement::{Top,Bottom,Left,Right}).show_arrow(bool).offset(px).radius(px).delay(ms).close_delay(ms).is_disabled().child(trigger)`
  - stateful: hover state lives in a per-tooltip `Window::use_keyed_state` entity, so `delay` / `closeDelay` work without the caller threading an entity through. Defaults come from the `--tooltip-delay` / `--tooltip-close-delay` theme tokens.
  - a generation counter invalidates a timer whose hover has already been superseded, which is what stops a fast pass across a row of triggers from opening all of them.
  - the key defaults to the tip text; give two tooltips with the same text distinct `id`s.

### Pickers
- **Autocomplete** — `Autocomplete::new(state, items).placement(Placement).max_items().radius(px).on_selection_change()` — filters while focused. Items are `PickerItem::new(key, label)`: v3 keeps a stable `Key` separate from the visible `textValue`, so `value` / `defaultValue` / `disabledKeys`, the selection callbacks and the form value address items by key, while filtering and the trigger's visible text use labels — duplicate labels never alias each other's selection or row. Value, option and empty-result text uses 14px/20px metrics; section headers use 12px/16px medium text. The popup anchors to the measured trigger with an 8px gap, flipping to the side with more room when the preferred side cannot fit and keeping a 12px cross-axis viewport inset with the scroller capped to the available height; the search stays visible while the inner list scrolls and shrinks to the available height within the upstream 320px max, and virtual paging follows the visible list height. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and it is the detached panel's corner — the panel's entry zoom interpolates the same value — while the trigger keeps the shared field chrome's own field radius.
  - `filter(fn(item_label, input) -> bool)` replaces the default case-insensitive substring match and owns the whole decision, including what an empty query means; `input_value` / `on_input_change` for a controlled query; `on_clear` is only the after-clear callback — the clear affordance is always mounted with the trigger, invisible and inert while the selection is empty or the field is disabled, and still working when read-only.
- **ComboBox** — `ComboBox::new(state, items).is_open().placement(Placement).menu_trigger(MenuTrigger::{Input,Manual,Focus}).allows_custom_value().max_items().radius(px).on_selection_change().on_open_change()` — items are keyed `PickerItem::new(key, label)`s: the selection, `disabledKeys`, the callbacks and the form value address items by key, while filtering and the input text use labels. `selected_keys(keys)` is the controlled ordered selection; `selected_key(key)` the single-key spelling (the empty string is v3's `null`). A committed custom value keeps the typed text and reports a null selected key — as an empty `on_selection_change_all` slice, and only when a selection actually existed; `form_value(ComboBoxFormValue::{Key,Text})` chooses what a named field submits (key by default — an empty selection still submits one empty value — and text under `allowsCustomValue`). Value, option and empty-result text uses 14px/20px metrics; section headers use 12px/16px medium text. When the preferred side cannot fit the popup, it flips to the side with more room, keeping a 12px cross-axis viewport inset with the scroller capped to the available height; plain and virtual lists use the available height with an 8px field gap, and wheel input stays in the list. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and it is the detached panel's corner — the panel's entry zoom interpolates the same value — while the trigger is the inner `Input`'s box and keeps the shared field chrome's own field radius.
- **Select** — `Select::new(id, options).selected(..)/.value(..).is_open().placement(Placement).variant().full_width().disabled_keys().is_invalid().is_required().radius(px).on_selection_change()/.on_change().on_open_change()`; `selection_mode(SelectionMode::Multiple)` with `selected_indices()` + `on_selection_change_all()`. `row_height(px)` is `ListLayout`'s `rowHeight` and what virtualizes the popup list through `uniform_list`: every option is exactly that tall, including the option box inside the row (it does not keep the 36px `.list-box-item` floor a plain list has). Enter and Space commit the highlighted option in single mode; if the selection callback closes the controlled popup, key release keeps it closed and leaves focus on the trigger. Value and option text uses 14px/20px metrics; section headers use 12px/16px medium text. `full_width(true)` expands both the root and trigger to the available container width. When the preferred side cannot fit the popup, it flips to the side with more room, keeping a 12px cross-axis viewport inset with the scroller capped to the available height; plain and virtual lists use the available height with an 8px trigger gap. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and it is the detached panel's corner — the panel's entry zoom interpolates the same value — while the trigger keeps the shared field chrome's own field radius.
  - The collection box seam: `Select` and `Autocomplete` accept `height(px)`, `padding_x(px)` and `is_bare(bool)` on the trigger, and every collection (`Select`, `ComboBox`, `Autocomplete`, `ListBox`) accepts `row_padding_x(px)` / `row_padding_y(px)` for its option rows, `row_hover_bg(color)` for the fill a hovered row takes, and `row_font_family(name)` for the detached popover rows, which do not inherit the trigger's font. Defaults are the stock metrics (`8/6` on ComboBox and ListBox, `10/6` on Select and Autocomplete). An explicit `height` fixes the trigger box, so content taller than it overflows; unset keeps the 36px minimum and grows with content; `ComboBox` forwards its three trigger builders to the inner `Input`, and `is_bare` drops only the paint while the list still opens and selects.

### Typography
The browser gallery bundles distinct Inter faces for Normal, Medium, Semibold and Bold weights.
- **Kbd** — `Kbd::new().variant(KbdVariant::{Default,Light}).radius(px).child("Ctrl")`
- **Typography** — `Typography::new(text).kind(TypographyType::{H1..H6,Body,BodySm,BodyXs,Code}).align().color(TextColor::{Default,Muted}).weight(FontWeight).font_family(name).truncate()`; helpers `heading(level, t)`, `paragraph(ParagraphSize, t)`, `code(t)`; `Prose::new()` for rich text

### Utilities
- **ScrollShadow** — `ScrollShadow::new(id).orientation().size(px).offset(px).visibility(ScrollShadowVisibility).is_enabled(bool).hide_scroll_bar(bool).max_h()/.max_w()`, `horizontal()` shorthand. v3's `variant` has one value. A painted overlay thumb uses `--scrollbar` unless `hide_scroll_bar` is set.
- **Scrollbar** — `Scrollbar::new(id, ScrollHandle).orientation()`. Overlay thumb painted from the theme token; auto-hides when the OS preference says so.
  - Wheel input scrolls only along the configured orientation.

## Gallery

`cargo run -p herogpui-gallery` — 1280×820 window, centred. `HEROGPUI_PAGE`
selects the page by nav title, `HEROGPUI_THEME=dark` selects the appearance,
`HEROGPUI_WINDOW_SIZE=1200x2000` sets the window size,
`HEROGPUI_UNFOCUSED=1` opens without taking focus, and
`HEROGPUI_REDUCE_MOTION=1` seeds the reduced-motion preference at startup
(see `gallery/src/main.rs`). Screenshots are the visual regression source.

## Code style

Pinned GPUI notes: `f32::from(px)` for `Pixels`, no `select_none`, `on_click`
and `.active()` need `.id()`, `svg()` never inherits text color, `Arc` for
shared callbacks, `.into_any_element()` for branch unification. Theme tokens are
already `Hsla` — never wrap them in `Hsla::from`. Divs are `Display::Block`, so
put controls in a flex parent or they stretch. Floating panels need
`util::floating` (`deferred`) to paint above later siblings. See `AGENTS.md`.

## Animation

v3 drives motion from data attributes; `crates/herogpui-components/src/anim.rs`
is the gpui equivalent and the single place the timings live.

- `anim::entering(el, id, cx)` — the `[data-entering]` 200ms ease-out fade, used
  by every overlay (Modal, Drawer, AlertDialog, Popover, Dropdown, Select,
  ComboBox, ColorPicker, Toast).
- `anim::entering_from(el, id, edge, travel, cx)` — adds the slide `Drawer` uses.
- `anim::pressed(el, PressBox { .. }, cx)` — v3's `[data-pressed]`
  `scale(0.97)`, applied by `Button` and `ToggleButton`, the two components v3
  documents it for.
- `anim::entering_zoom(el, id, ZoomBox { .. }, cx)` — v3's `[data-entering]` in
  full: `zoom-in-90 fade-in-0 duration-200`. Used by every overlay; the backdrop
  fades alongside it.
- `anim::exiting(el, id, ZoomBox, cx)` / `exiting_to(..)` — v3's
  `[data-exiting]`: `animate-out zoom-out-95 fade-out duration-150`, and the
  drawer's `slide-out-to-*`. A `RenderOnce` component leaves the tree the moment
  `isOpen` goes false, so `util::overlay_phase` holds it for `EXITING_MS` first:
  it returns `Closed` / `Open` / `Exiting`, and the caller picks the animation.
- `anim::hover_fade(el, id, idle, hovered, window, cx)` — v3's
  `transition-colors`. gpui has no property transitions, so the element keeps its
  own hover flag and generation counter and each change eases the fill in OKLab.
- `anim::caret_blink(el, id, cx)` — v3's `@keyframes caret-blink`, on the text
  and OTP carets.
- `anim::Motion` — the duration, scale and `Curve` v3 declares per overlay:
  `PANEL_IN` (250ms `ease-out-quad`, from **1.05** — a modal settles *down* onto
  the page), `BACKDROP_IN` (150ms `ease-out`, fade only), `POPOVER_IN` (150ms
  `ease-smooth`, 0.90), `LIST_IN` (150ms, 0.95), `FLUID_IN` (250ms
  `ease-out-fluid`, 0.95), `DRAWER_IN`/`DRAWER_OUT` (250/200ms `ease-out-fluid`),
  and a `*_OUT` for each at 100ms. `anim::Curve` evaluates v3's `--ease-*`
  cubic-beziers exactly, rather than substituting one of gpui's two built-ins.
- `anim::ENTERING_MS` (150), `EXITING_MS` (100), `TRANSITION_MS` (100),
  `PRESS_MS` (250 — recorded, since gpui's `active` has no timeline to ramp
  along), `PRESSED_SCALE`, `anim::pressed_inset`.
- **Reduced motion:** `ActiveTheme::reduce_motion(cx)` gates every animation with no opt-in
  from the caller. Set it with `theme::set_reduce_motion(bool, cx)` or
  `theme::toggle_reduce_motion(cx)`; `HEROGPUI_REDUCE_MOTION=1` seeds it at
  startup. The value is stored in GPUI's own `App::reduce_motion()` global, so a
  plain `gpui::Animation` written by the app is suppressed too, and either
  accessor reads the same flag.

**No div transforms.** the pinned GPUI plumbs `TransformationMatrix` into
`paint_svg` alone, so quads and text cannot be scaled or rotated. Two
consequences — both worked around geometrically rather than left undone:

- The press is **geometric** rather than a transform: `PressBox` scales the
  height, padding, gap, corner radius, minimum width **and type size** by 0.97,
  with margins absorbing exactly what the box gives up, so the outer footprint
  is identical (pressing never nudges a neighbour) while the visible box
  contracts about its centre. Scaling the type is what makes this a real scale
  rather than an inset — gpui accepts fractional font sizes, so the glyphs
  shrink with the box. Two differences from a CSS transform remain: a label
  wider than the control's `min_w` narrows the control by ~3% of that overflow,
  because gpui cannot shrink text without affecting layout; and an icon child
  keeps its size, since its dimensions belong to the caller. `Toast`'s
  `scaleFactor` shrinks stacked toasts the same way, by insetting their width.
- The overlay entry's `zoom-in-90` uses the same technique: `ZoomBox` grows the
  panel's width, padding, type size and corner radius from 90% while it fades
  in. What a real `scale()` would also carry, and this does not, is a child
  whose size the caller fixed — an icon or image inside the panel keeps its
  size while the chrome around it grows.
